summary: Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Ernst Steinkellner and taught Geshe Yeshe Tobden. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at the Vidyadhara Institute (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. Educated at the University of the Punjab and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and Raghu Vira, he held long-term leadership posts at the International Academy of Indian Culture, ICCR, and ICHR.
Longlian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai Shi from circa 1941 to 1967.

Lore Sander specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Ernst Waldschmidt. She held posts at the Museum of Asian Art, Free University of Berlin, Humboldt University of Berlin, and University of Munich.

A scholar of Buddhist, Japanese, and religious studies, Lori Meeks earned degrees at Columbia and Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. Following a postdoctoral fellowship at Stanford, she joined the University of Southern California in 2005 as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies.

Lorna Dewaraja was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London, and held faculty posts at the University of Peradeniya, University of Colombo, and St Anne's College.

A scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies, Lothar Ledderose studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Princeton, Tokyo, Harvard, and Cologne. He served as professor at Heidelberg University (1976–2010) and was president of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

Lothar von Falkenhausen, a specialist in archaeology and Sinology, studied at Bonn, Peking University, and Harvard. Since 1993 he has served as professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was associate director there from 2004 to 2011.

Louis Dumont specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying under Marcel Mauss, Walther Schubring, and Alain Froment. He held positions at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires, University of Oxford, and the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales.

Louis Finot, an Indologist and historian educated at the École des Chartes, was the first director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from 1898 and held a chair at the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who held a position at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1977 to 2007.

Louis H. Gray worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Princeton and Columbia, he held posts at Princeton University (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (1921).

Louis Havet was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and chair of Latin philology at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

Indologist and linguist Louis Renou studied under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch at EPHE and Paris. He held professorships and directorships at the University of Lyon, EPHE, Sorbonne University, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and the Institut de civilisation indienne.

Louis de La Vallée Poussin was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Liège, Leuven, and Leiden under Sylvain Lévi and Hendrik Kern. He served as professor at Ghent University (1893–1929) and the Free University of Brussels (1921–1935).

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Indology and Iranian studies, studying at the Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy. He served as Chief Keeper of Manuscripts at the Bibliothèque nationale and founded and directed the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Louise Allison Cort, a specialist in Japanology and archaeology, studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College. She served as ceramics curator at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries from circa 1981 to 2020.
Louise Child is a religious studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Leeds and studied under Ringu Tulku. She held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University under Sibnath Sarma (attested 1999) and also studied under S. Shyamkishor Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.
